metadata.description: Intercontinental supply chain of lithium: from brine extraction in the Atacama Desert (Chile) via the Panama Canal to battery cathode manufacturing in Germany.
primary_sources: USGS (U.S. Geological Survey) Lithium Mineral Commodity Summaries
Federal Institute for Geosciences and Natural Resources (BGR)

properties.name: Salar de Atacama (Chile)
properties.capacity: approx. 180,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) / year
properties.summary: The world’s richest lithium deposit, in South America’s ‘Lithium Triangle’.
properties.description: Located at 2,300 metres altitude. Lithium-bearing brine is pumped to the surface from underground reservoirs and concentrated over months in huge evaporation ponds by the intense sunshine of the Atacama Desert.

aha_moment.title: From salt lake to your smartphone
aha_moment.explanation: Every smartphone contains about 2 to 3 grams of pure lithium, an electric car battery between 8 and 12 kilograms. Nearly half of the world’s reserves lie here in the Chilean Andes.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Provides the cordless energy for modern laptops, electric cars and energy storage.

properties.name: Port of Antofagasta (Pacific coast, Chile)
properties.capacity: Central Pacific export hub for Chilean minerals
properties.summary: The world’s gateway for lithium and copper exports overseas.
properties.description: This is where the dried and refined white lithium carbonate powder is loaded into containers and onto cargo ships for transport to Europe and Asia.

aha_moment.title: Starting point of a 12,000 km sea voyage
aha_moment.explanation: Cargo ships loaded with thousands of tonnes of ‘white gold’ set sail from here to cross the oceans and supply the European car industry with battery cell materials.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Links the driest desert on Earth with Germany’s high-tech factories.

properties.name: Port of Hamburg (Container Terminal Altenwerder)
properties.capacity: Germany’s largest seaport for special and container cargo
properties.summary: Germany’s gateway for intercontinental battery raw materials.
properties.description: Container ships from South America unload here. The lithium is transferred from ocean vessels to freight trains and inland barges that take it straight to the new battery plants in eastern Germany.
consumer_products: Import handling of battery raw materials

aha_moment.title: From ocean giant to rail
aha_moment.explanation: State-of-the-art automated cranes lift the containers from ship to freight train within minutes, ensuring a seamless supply chain for electric mobility.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Without the Port of Hamburg, production of German electric vehicles would come to a halt.

properties.name: BASF Schwarzheide battery materials centre (Lusatia)
properties.capacity: Cathode material for approx. 400,000 electric vehicles / year
properties.summary: Europe’s most modern large-scale production of cathode active materials (CAM) and battery recycling.
properties.description: In Schwarzheide (Brandenburg), BASF synthesises high-purity cathode materials from imported lithium, nickel, cobalt and manganese. They are delivered directly to European battery cell makers such as ACC and CATL and to German carmakers.
consumer_products: Lithium-ion battery cells for electric cars
Home storage batteries for solar systems

aha_moment.title: The chemical heart of the transport transition
aha_moment.explanation: The cathode material largely determines the range, charging speed and lifetime of modern electric cars. Here, Chilean salt is turned into high technology.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Your next electric car or the solar battery in your basement uses material refined right here.

properties.name: Transoceanic lithium route (Chile → Panama Canal → Hamburg)
properties.flow_direction: Antofagasta (Chile) → Pacific → Panama Canal → North Atlantic → Hamburg
properties.summary: Intercontinental deep-sea transport artery for the global energy transition.
properties.description: Covers almost 13,000 kilometres: from the Pacific through the locks of the Panama Canal into the Caribbean, across the North Atlantic and through the North Sea straight into the Elbe estuary to Hamburg.

aha_moment.title: 13,000 km by sea for one battery charge
aha_moment.explanation: Before the battery of an electric car assembled in Germany is charged for the first time, its raw materials have already travelled halfway around the world on cargo ships.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Illustrates the enormous global division of labour – and dependence – behind modern future technologies.

source.name: World Shipping Council / BGR raw materials report

properties.name: Rail freight corridor Hamburg – Schwarzheide
properties.summary: Electrified rail corridor for onward transport from the seaport to the plant.
properties.description: Connects the Port of Hamburg directly with the rail siding of the Schwarzheide industrial park and the Berlin-Brandenburg region.
consumer_products: Inland logistics for battery raw materials

aha_moment.title: Low-emission transport right to the factory gate
aha_moment.explanation: A single freight train replaces up to 52 trucks on the A24 and A13 motorways and brings the raw material directly to the chemical reactor.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Secures just-in-time production without traffic jams on the roads.

properties.name: Atacama → Antofagasta Lithium Corridor
properties.operator: Mining operators / Chilean logistics (e.g. SQM, Albemarle supply chains)
properties.capacity: Concentrated lithium products to export port
properties.summary: Land transport corridor from the Salar de Atacama brine operations to the Pacific export port of Antofagasta.
properties.description: Lithium carbonate and related products produced at the Salar de Atacama are moved by road and rail roughly 200–250 km west to the port of Antofagasta. From there they are loaded onto ships for the intercontinental route to Europe.
properties.flow_direction: Salar de Atacama → Port of Antofagasta → Ocean vessels

aha_moment.title: From desert brine to the Pacific
aha_moment.explanation: After lithium is extracted from the salt flats, it still has to cross the desert to the coast. Only then does the long sea journey to Europe begin.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Every lithium shipment that later arrives in Hamburg has first travelled this short but essential desert corridor.

source.name: Chilean mining & port logistics / open data
